title: Several behavioral tests never assert the computed result
reasoning: These scenarios exercise nested expression counting and waste detection for method calls and decorated functions, but do not check their results. They pass when the relevant counts or classifications are wrong, provided execution does not raise. In particular, the nested-expression test unpacks both counters without asserting either, leaving its stated distinction between top-level and total expressions unprotected.
reproduction: For the nested-expression scenario, substitute any two incorrect numeric counts: the test still passes. Likewise, changing the waste classifications returned for the method-call and decorated-function scenarios cannot fail their existing assertions because there are none.
recommendation: Extend these existing scenarios with assertions on the intended counters and classifications. Include positive and negative cases so the tests distinguish correct detection from constant or empty results.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: Nearby expression tests only check a lower bound on total expressions; these scenarios do not verify the top-level/total distinction. The cited waste scenarios discard the returned metrics. Other supplied waste tests cover ordinary and recursive functions, but do not assert these method-call and decorated-function outcomes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Assert both expression counters for the existing nested fixture, then vary nesting while preserving the total number of calls. Extend the method and decorated-function fixtures across one and multiple call sites and assert the corresponding single-use classifications.
minimumFixScope: Existing scenarios in tests/metrics/language/py_symbols_test.py and tests/metrics/language/py_waste_test.py.
